compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`process_snapshot` (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`) copies every key of a SNAPSHOT's
`compiled_state` into reduced state, and ordinary replay starts at the latest SNAPSHOT.
Any ticket compacted after a forced close was followed by reopen (bug 6df4-d3f0, fixed in
the reducer fold) has the stale `force_close_reason` / `close_class` / `close_reason` /
`completion_expectation` frozen into its SNAPSHOT. Fixing the fold and bumping the reducer
cache version does not reach these: replay never re-folds the retired source events.

## Evidence (this repo's tracker, 2026-10-18)

- 8 SNAPSHOTs with `status: closed`, a `force_close_reason`, and `last_reopened_at` set,
  whose most recent closing STATUS event carried no force reason (e.g. aabf-d89e,
  a8ea-be28, ad81-73ad, 3d7a-7795, 7332-a728, a881-2d9a, 52b0-6a6a, 14f4-d616).
- 4 SNAPSHOTs with status open/in_progress still carrying `force_close_reason`
  (76b2-4b5f, 075b-1479, 84e6-0fda, e215-ab23).

## Approach to decide in plan review

`rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact_rebuild.py`) already
recomputes a SNAPSHOT from the full log including `*.retired` sources, under the write
lock with a crash-safe sentinel. A one-shot idempotent migration in the ensure-registry
(`docs/migrations.md`) could select tickets whose SNAPSHOT carries `force_close_reason`
and `last_reopened_at` and rebuild them. This mutates the shared tracker, so it is split
from the pure reducer fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every SNAPSHOT whose compiled close metadata disagrees with a full-log reduction is
  rebuilt; a fixture store with a stale closed SNAPSHOT reduces with no `force_close_reason`.
- [ ] The migration is idempotent (second run makes no writes).

## Testing
```
.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit -k snapshot_close_metadata -q
```
compiled_state.title: Compacted SNAPSHOTs bake in stale force_close_reason from a pre-reopen forced close
